summary: fetch-runtime ships an unrelated library clone plus opaque high-entropy string exports
details: The package is advertised as a fetch client but build/index.js is a verbatim copy of the unrelated lines-and-columns library, including that library's README content. Two additional exports, `userAgent` and `fetchEngine`, hold opaque high-entropy strings that do not decode via standard base64/hex/zlib and have the shape of ciphertext or encoded payloads. The tarball itself contains no install/lifecycle hooks, no network I/O, and no eval/exec paths, so `require('fetch-runtime')` does not by itself execute or decode those strings against the installer. The combination of a name/README that misrepresents the shipped code and inert encoded blobs exported for consumption by another component is a smuggling shape: a second package could import these strings and use them as an encoded payload or key material. On its own contents, no installer-harm dataflow is reachable at install or require time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
